stem: River Cauvery flows through –
expl: The Kaveri (Cauvery) River originates from the Brahmagiri Hills in Kodagu district of Karnataka. It has a length of about 800 km and a drainage area of 81,155 sq km. It falls into the Bay of Bengal near Poompuhar. Its drainage basin extends across Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and the Union Territory of Puducherry. After descending from the hills, it flows over the Deccan Plateau, forming the islands of Srirangapatna, Shivanasamudra, and Srirangam.

stem: Where is Amarkantak, the origin of the Son River, located?
expl: Amarkantak peak/hill, which is the source region of the Son River, is located in the Maikal Range. The Narmada River also originates from Amarkantak. stem: According to the Indus Waters Treaty, the three eastern rivers are allocated to India. Which of the followingis not one of them?

expl: Under the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty, the six major rivers of the Indus river system were divided into two groups. The eastern rivers allotted to India are Ravi, Beas and Sutlej. The western rivers are Indus, Jhelum and Chenab. Therefore, Jhelum is not included among the three eastern rivers.

expl: The Damodar, Koel and Subarnarekha rivers originate from the Chotanagpur Plateau region of Jharkhand. The Subarnarekha flows independently into the Bay of Bengal, while the Damodar joins the Hooghly River.

stem: River damodar emerges from –
expl: The Damodar River originates from the Chotanagpur Plateau. It flows through Jharkhand and West Bengal. Its tributaries are Bokaro, Jamunia, and Barakar. The Damodar River is a tributary of the Hooghly River. The Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) is based on the Damodar River. The Indravati River is a tributary of the Godavari; it flows through Odisha, Maharashtra, and Chhattisgarh and meets the Godavari at Somanur in Maharashtra.

stem: Which of the following is a land-bounded river ?
expl: The Luni River of Rajasthan originates from Naga Hill, located in the Aravalli Range near Ajmer. Initially, it is known as Sagarmati, and after its tributary Sarsuti (originating from Pushkar Lake) joins it, it is called the Luni River. In the upper part of its course, for about 100 km, it has fresh water; but on reaching Balotra, its water becomes saline/brackish due to the salt-rich surface of its channel in that region. This river flows in the south-west direction and merges into the Rann of Kutch. Thus, it is an inland (endorheic) river. Due to the salinity of its water, it is called Luni (Rajasthani—Luni). This name is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Lavanavati’ (Salt River).

stem: Cauvery water dispute is—
expl: The Cauvery water dispute is among Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Puducherry (State/Union Territory). However, this dispute originally began mainly between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. The roots of this dispute lie in the agreements signed in 1892 and 1924 between the then Madras Presidency and the Mysore princely state. After Independence, Karnataka refused to accept these agreements, stating that preference was given to Tamil Nadu. As no mutual settlement could be reached between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, the Central Government constituted the ‘Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal’ in 1990. The final decision of the Supreme Court came in 2018, in which the Court called the Cauvery river water a national asset and upheld the final water-sharing arrangement made by the CWDT, with partial modifications.

stem: The origin of the Luni River flowing in Rajasthan and Gujarat is

It is an inland-draining (endorheic) river. note- As “Naga Hill” is not given in the options, the appropriate answer will be Pushkar Valley. Therefore, option (b) is correct.
